_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the friend-facing TTW client package. Every version and hash here was verified against the host's own staged files on 2026-09-15. Do not bump a version without re-hashing: NV:MP kicks any player whose ESM/ESP set does not match the host byte-for-byte, so version drift between host and friend is a hard failure, not a cosmetic one.

pack.name: Poosic's Wasteland
pack.packNote: Tale of Two Wastelands 3.4 + YUPTTW + NV:MP co-op client.

server.name: Poosic's Wasteland
server.hostNote: Albert's public IP. It is a DHCP lease and CAN change on a fiber re-lease. The installer always reads this value from the published manifest at run time, never from a value compiled into the exe, so a re-lease is fixed by re-publishing this file - friends do not reinstall.
server.serverBinaryNote: NV:MP co-op is PEER-HOSTED: the server exe runs from inside the host's own Fallout New Vegas folder, alongside the exact same mods. It is not a standalone dedicated server.

prereqs.diskFreeNote: TTW's own installer asks for 17 GB free at its destination; on the host, the files written by today's build (modified in the 3 hours before the check, not the TTW folder total) came to 16.1 GB. 45 GB leaves room for the 1.2 GB download, the extracted installer and the build.
prereqs.refuseProgramFilesNote: MO2's virtual filesystem and xNVSE both break under the UAC-protected Program Files tree. If either game lives there the installer stops and tells the player how to move it, because the failure mode otherwise appears hours later as a silent crash.

steamApps.name: Fallout 3 - Game of the Year Edition
steamApps.requiredFilesNote: All five FO3 DLC are MANDATORY - TTW is built against every one of them and the installer aborts partway through without them. appid 22300 is plain Fallout 3; it only qualifies if the player bought the DLC separately, so the DLC file check is what actually decides, not the appid.

steamApps.name: Fallout: New Vegas
steamApps.requiredFilesNote: All four story DLC, GRA, and the four pre-order packs. TTW's load order expects every one of them present and in this order.

components.name: xNVSE
components.note: Script extender. Goes loose in the FNV root, NOT through MO2. Verified: the GitHub asset is 5,648,605 bytes, byte-identical in size to the host's staged copy.

components.name: Mod Organizer 2
components.note: OPTIONAL AND OFF BY DEFAULT - deliberately not on the install path. NV:MP launches its own process and therefore cannot see Mod Organizer's virtual filesystem, so mods staged behind the VFS are invisible to it and produce exactly the 'Invalid mod revisions' kick this pack exists to prevent. NV:MP's own README is explicit that the server 'must be ran alongside your current Fallout installation'. This pack installs straight into the real Data folder so the host and every friend are structurally identical. Kept here only for players who separately want MO2 for single-player modding. Verified: GitHub asset size 149,660,212 matches the host's staged copy exactly.

components.name: FNV 4GB Patcher
components.downloadHint: On the Files tab take the one called "4GB Patcher" (v1.5, 102 KB) - NOT "FNV4GB for Linux".
components.note: REQUIRED. Stock New Vegas has 2 GB of address space and TTW crashes it. Setting the flag by hand breaks Steam's DRM ('Application load error 3:0000065432', seen on the host), so this patcher is the only safe way. NV:MP's Getting Started page lists it as required. Nexus Mods requires a free account to download, so this is a manual download: setup opens the page, finds the file in Downloads/Desktop/Documents, and verifies it.

components.name: Tale of Two Wastelands
components.fetchNote: MANUAL ON PURPOSE - this is a legal constraint, not a technical one. Bethesda asked mod sites not to host TTW and required the custom installer specifically so Fallout 3's assets are never redistributed; TTW is therefore published only from its own site and ModPub. This package NEVER mirrors it. The installer opens the official page, waits for the player's own download, then verifies the SHA-256 above so a truncated or wrong-version file is caught before it wastes an hour.
components.installerNote: The TTW installer is a Delphi GUI whose ONLY command-line switch is -NoOggEnc2. There is no silent or unattended mode, so this one step is necessarily player-driven; the installer pre-validates both game paths and shows the exact values to enter, then verifies the output.

components.name: TTW OGG Vorbis libraries
components.note: Three DLLs that replace FNV's stock Vorbis libs in the game root. Needed for TTW's converted audio; without them FO3-side dialogue is silent.

components.name: YUP - TTW patch
components.note: Ships YUPTTW.esm plus Main/Sounds BSAs and their .override markers. Extracted straight into the Fallout New Vegas Data folder, on top of the TTW output, so NV:MP sees it in the real game folder rather than behind a mod manager.

components.name: NV:MP co-op client
components.note: Official distribution is NVMP/ClientDistribution on GitHub (named by the NV:MP wiki's Hosting_TTW page), so this is fetched automatically. The launcher self-updates the CLIENT but NOT nvmp_storyserver.exe - on 2026-09-23 the host's launcher jumped 9.0->9.2 while the server stayed 9.0. So the server version here must track the newest client: when NV:MP ships a new build, bump this and update the host's server too. Contains nvmp_storyserver.exe, which only the HOST runs.

components.name: NVTF - New Vegas Tick Fix
components.downloadHint: Main file "NVTF". You ALSO need the separate "NVTF - INI" file from the same page.
components.note: Engine stability fix. The host crashed repeatedly under NV:MP (FalloutNV.exe+0x282303, memory corruption) until NVTF was installed; NV:MP itself logs 'NVTF is not present!' without it. NV:MP's server registers NVSE plugins, so host and players carry the same set. Nexus Mods requires a free account to download, so this is a manual download: setup opens the page, finds the file in Downloads/Desktop/Documents, and verifies it.

components.name: NVTF - INI
components.downloadHint: The small "NVTF - INI" file on NVTF's Files tab.
components.note: NVTF refuses to run without it ('NVTF.ini not found'); it is a separate download so updates never overwrite it. Default settings. Nexus Mods requires a free account to download, so this is a manual download: setup opens the page, finds the file in Downloads/Desktop/Documents, and verifies it.

components.name: JohnnyGuitar NVSE
components.note: TTW 3.4 checks for it at startup ('JohnnyGuitar is missing or outdated'). Official GitHub release, fetched automatically.

components.name: ShowOff xNVSE
components.note: TTW 3.4 checks for it at startup. Official GitHub release, fetched automatically.

components.name: JIP LN NVSE Plugin
components.downloadHint: Main file "JIP LN NVSE Plugin" (v57.30). Also take "JIP LN Settings INI" from the same page.
components.note: TTW 3.4 requires 57.21+ ('JIP LN NVSE Plugin is missing or you are using a version older than 57.21'). JIP also provides the FalloutCustom.ini feature setup relies on. Nexus requires a free account, so this is a manual download; setup finds it by name OR by size+fingerprint, so a renamed download still works.

components.name: JIP LN Settings INI
components.downloadHint: The small "JIP LN Settings INI" file on JIP's Files tab.
components.note: JIP's settings, as the Best of Times guide installs them. Nexus requires a free account, so this is a manual download; setup finds it by name OR by size+fingerprint, so a renamed download still works.

components.name: TTW NVSE Plugin (ROOGNVSE)
components.note: TTW's own NVSE plugin; TTW 3.4 checks for it at startup. Nexus requires a free account, so this is a manual download; setup finds it by name OR by size+fingerprint, so a renamed download still works.

components.name: lStewieAl's Tweaks and Engine Fixes
components.downloadHint: Main file "lStewieAl's Tweaks" (v10.00) and "Stewie Tweaks INI". NOT the optional extras (Perk Per Level, Quick Scope Anims) - they change gameplay and would differ from everyone else.
components.note: TTW 3.4 checks for it at startup. Nexus names this download unusually (a random suffix), hence the fingerprint matching. Nexus requires a free account, so this is a manual download; setup finds it by name OR by size+fingerprint, so a renamed download still works.

components.name: Stewie Tweaks INI
components.downloadHint: The small "Stewie Tweaks INI" file on the Tweaks page.
components.note: A stub the plugin fills in with defaults on first launch; keepExisting so re-running setup never wipes the filled-in file. Nexus requires a free account, so this is a manual download; setup finds it by name OR by size+fingerprint, so a renamed download still works.

loadOrderNote: The parity contract: NV:MP kicks any player whose active plugins differ from the host. 18 plugins, EXACTLY the list on NV:MP's own wiki page Hosting_TTW (nuwiki.nv-mp.com, read 2026-09-23), so anyone who set TTW up by that guide matches too. The six FO3 plugins are hard masters of TaleOfTwoWastelands.esm (read from its TES4 header). In New Vegas the ORDER comes from file timestamps, which setup stamps to match this list.

parity.esmSourceNote: TaleOfTwoWastelands.esm is BUILT on each player's machine from their own Fallout 3 files - it is never shipped. Parity therefore depends entirely on every player feeding the installer the SAME pinned inputs: TTW 3.4.0 build 2026.06.11 and YUPTTW 13.9.1. Identical inputs produce an identical ESM, which is what satisfies NV:MP. This is the whole reason the hashes above are pinned rather than 'latest'.

ttwOutput._comment: Recorded from the host's clean TTW 3.4 build (-NoOggEnc2) on 2026-09-23. sha256 = the parity check: those plugins must be byte-identical to the host's or NV:MP kicks the player. Verified deterministic - two separate builds on the host (2026-09-06 and 2026-09-23) produced identical hashes for all seven built plugins. YUPTTW.esm is the pinned 13.9.1 file, which setup lays over the older copy TTW bundles. files = host BSA sizes, used only as a completeness floor (a build must reach 95% of each): the host's first build stopped with TaleOfTwoWastelands - Main.bsa at 1.2 MB of 1,065 MB, and a floor catches that without failing a friend over a small legitimate size difference.

gameSettings._comment: Applied to Documents\My Games\FalloutNV by setup. Each fixed or guards against a crash seen on the host 2026-09-23. sIntroMovie is set in BOTH files: FalloutPrefs.ini also carries it and overrides Fallout.ini. Resolution is not listed: setup picks a 16:9 size for the player's own screen.

customIni._comment: Written verbatim to Documents\My Games\FalloutNV\FalloutCustom.ini. These are the Tale of Two Wastelands settings from The Best of Times guide (Essential Mods > Custom INI) - the file NV:MP's own Hosting_TTW page says to copy. Read by JIP LN NVSE and overrides the other INIs. Without it TTW warns 'Misconfigured INI settings' and SCharGenQuest (TTW's starting quest) is unset. Verified in-game on the host 2026-09-23. Live-editable: no rebuild needed.
customIni.content:
; Written by Dojo Setup - the Tale of Two Wastelands settings from The Best of Times guide
; (thebestoftimes.moddinglinked.com, Essential Mods > Custom INI). Read by JIP LN NVSE;
; overrides the other game INIs without editing them. TTW warns "Misconfigured INI settings" without it.
